title: Aadhaar, PAN, Passport and RTI: Your Rights
summary: When a document is required by law, how to fix mistakes, report misuse, and use the Right to Information (RTI).

body.text: Identity documents prove who you are. They help you get services. If you know when a document is needed by law, and how to fix problems, you are safe from fraud and from people troubling you.

items: Aadhaar: a 12-digit number. It proves who you are. It does not prove you are an Indian citizen.
PAN: needed for income tax. Also needed for many money dealings above certain limits.
Voter ID (EPIC): proves you are registered to vote in your area.
Passport: proves who you are and that you are a citizen. Mainly used for travel.
Driving licence: proves you can drive a certain type of vehicle.

body.text: When a document is needed by law, and when it is not

items: Aadhaar is usually needed for PAN, for many subsidies, and for KYC (identity checks). But it is not needed for every single service.
If the law does not link a service to Aadhaar, no one can demand your Aadhaar. Ask them to show the rule in writing.
For many private needs, a photocopy is enough. Do not give your original documents casually.
You can ask to fix mistakes in Aadhaar, PAN or the voter list. Use the official website or office.
If someone misuses your identity, tell the police and the office that gave the document.
If it is a money fraud, call 1930 and report on cybercrime.gov.in on the same day.
You can check where your Aadhaar was used (authentication history). You can also lock your biometrics (fingerprint and eye scan) online.
Any citizen can ask a government office for information. This is done by filing an RTI application.
The office must usually reply within 30 days.
If they refuse or ignore you, you can file a first appeal. After that, you can file a second appeal to the Information Commission.

body.text: Be careful of fake officials and copy websites. Real government websites end with .gov.in or .nic.in. Never pay a 'processing fee' to a personal account or a UPI ID.
You can lock your Aadhaar biometrics online. Then no one can use them until you unlock them.
Keep only the copies you need. Never post photos of your Aadhaar, PAN or passport on social media.

practicalSteps: Download or update documents only from official websites like uidai.gov.in, incometax.gov.in, nvsp.in and passportindia.gov.in.
Where it is accepted, use masked Aadhaar (only the last 4 digits are shown).
If a document is misused, file a police complaint and an online report on the same day.
If you have a problem with a government service, file an RTI or a complaint (grievance) on the department's website.
exceptions: Some services are linked to Aadhaar by law. Asking Aadhaar for those services is legal. For others, it is not.
RTI does not cover some secret matters. For example, national security and a person's private details.

faqs.q: Can a shop or hotel demand my Aadhaar?
faqs.a: Only if the law links that service to Aadhaar. If not, you can say no and show another accepted ID.

faqs.q: How do I know a government website is real?
faqs.a: Check the website address. Official sites use .gov.in or .nic.in and have a valid https certificate. Type the address yourself. Do not click links.

sources.label: Right to Information Act, 2005 - India Code

misconceptions.myth: Aadhaar proves I am an Indian citizen.
misconceptions.fact: Aadhaar proves who you are. It does not prove citizenship. Citizenship is shown by other documents like a passport.
